original_description: How to read an authorised web pentest engagement in SurfaceWatch, the local console that captures web apps' client-side attack surface (endpoints, parameters, statuses, security headers, scripts, third-party origins) and compares captures between builds. Read this skill before calling any surfacewatch tool (overview, list_captures, get_surface, diff, list_findings, get_finding, readiness), because it has the scope rules, how to treat flags and recorded data, and how to lay out a surface diff or finding summary. Use it whenever the user mentions SurfaceWatch, an engagement, target, capture, baseline or finding ID (F-001), or asks what changed in a target's surface between builds, which endpoints or third-party origins are new, which security headers are missing, what a capture flagged, which findings to retest, or why captures fail.
best_description: SurfaceWatch skill: read it first, before ToolSearch or any mcp__surfacewatch__ tool, even when the tools look enough on their own. The server's instructions leave out the scope and test-window rules, how to handle recorded data and flags, and the report layout for diffs and findings. Use it for any request that reads the user's own pentest records, whether or not SurfaceWatch is named: listing engagements, test windows or targets; comparing a new client build or today's capture with the baseline or an earlier crawl (new or removed endpoints, parameters, statuses, headers, scripts, third-party origins); deciding which findings to retest; summarising a finding (F-001) and its evidence for a report; and fixing failed captures or checking REA, Node.js or Chromium setup. Skip it for scanning or exploiting a live host, code review, payloads, and general pentest knowledge or documents. SurfaceWatch only reads captures that were already recorded.

history.description: Use this skill whenever a question can be answered from the user's own pentest engagement data, even if they don't name SurfaceWatch (the local pentest console). This covers engagements and their test windows, targets, captures or crawls and the baseline, a target's attack surface (endpoints, parameters, statuses, security headers, scripts, third-party origins), what changed after a new build or since an earlier capture, and findings (F-007) with their evidence and retests. It also covers captures that fail, or REA, Node or Chromium setup. Load it before the first mcp__surfacewatch__ call (overview, diff, get_surface, list_findings, get_finding, readiness). It has the scope rules and the report layout that the tools leave out. Don't use it to scan, crawl or exploit a live URL, or for general security questions, because SurfaceWatch only reads captures that were already recorded.
